biggest_catch: This is for musicians with music to sell, not resellers — you need original recordings or merch, and the buyers are fans, not bargain hunters.
catches: Official revenue share: 15% digital, 10% physical goods; payment processing separate (~4–7% on average purchases).
Artists keep roughly 80–85% of a typical purchase; paid out daily.
Artist accounts are free; Bandcamp Pro ($10/mo) is optional for marketing tools.
Bandcamp Fridays waive the revenue share entirely — 2026 schedule: Sep 4, Oct 2, Nov 6, Dec 4.
Pay-what-you-want pricing: fans routinely pay 50%+ above the minimum.
Sales volume depends on your audience — no audience, no sales; this is direct-to-fan, not discovery.

eligibility: Musicians/artists with recordings or merch to sell
maximize: Time major releases for Bandcamp Fridays (Sep 4, Oct 2, Nov 6, Dec 4, 2026) — you keep ~97% instead of ~82%, so save your biggest drop for the nearest Friday. Use pay-what-you-want minimums: fans pay 50%+ above minimums on average, so set a low floor and let generosity work. Build your follower list on the platform — followers get notified of new releases, and that's your free marketing channel. Bundle merch with digital downloads (vinyl/CD + instant download) to raise average order value. This is the rare platform where the audience pays MORE than asking, so invest in the relationship: liner notes, bonus tracks, and personal messages drive repeat buying.
notes: Grounded on Bandcamp official Fair Trade Music Policy (archived 2023 official page; fee text unchanged per 2026 reporting): 15% revenue share on digital, 10% on merchandise, processing separate, artists receive ~82% average paid daily. Current applicability confirmed by 2026 reporting: Bandcamp Fridays scheduled for Sept 4, Oct 2, Nov 6, Dec 4, 2026 with zero revenue share (~97% to artist minus processing). Creator-direct lane (original music/merch) — adds breadth, not a resale flip.

s6.note: 4 steps: create artist page, upload releases, set price, get paid daily.

steps: Create a free Bandcamp artist page and upload your music/merch
Set fixed, minimum, or pay-what-you-want pricing
Promote to your audience; time releases for Bandcamp Fridays
Receive daily payouts minus 15% (digital) / 10% (merch) plus processing
who_pays: Your fans pay you through Bandcamp, and Bandcamp disburses your earnings daily.
who_qualifies: Musicians and artists with recordings or merch to sell.
work_available: Bandcamp is active and open to artist accounts (free accounts available; Bandcamp Pro at $10/mo is optional). Bandcamp Fridays waive the revenue share entirely (2026 schedule: Sep 4, Oct 2, Nov 6, Dec 4).
what_gets_accepted: Your music or merch is sold directly to fans — pay-what-you-want pricing is standard, and fans routinely pay 50%+ above the minimum. Sales volume depends on your audience: no audience, no sales — this is direct-to-fan, not discovery.
costs_and_unpaid_time: Official revenue share: 15% digital, 10% physical goods; payment processing is separate (~4–7% on average purchases). Artists keep roughly 80–85% of a typical purchase. Unpaid time goes to uploading music, setting prices, and building your audience.
when_cash_arrives: Daily payouts — Bandcamp pays out your earnings every day.
